social_circle.name: Linda Barham

demographics.occupation: Retired medical billing specialist (formerly at a small primary care practice in Amsterdam, NY)
demographics.location: Amsterdam, NY (south side, ~15 minutes from Rickey)
demographics.education: Associate's degree in business administration, Fulton-Montgomery Community College

background.how_they_met: Mother and son — Linda gave birth to Rickey on March 14, 1995 in Amsterdam, NY; raised him as an only child in a ranch house off Route 30 with husband Wayne.
background.why_close: Linda is the surviving parent after Wayne's sudden death in 2018; she and Rickey have built a tight, predictable rhythm around Sunday dinners and weekday phone calls, and Rickey handles her home repairs and tech needs in exchange for casseroles and roasts. Their bond deepened during her spring-2024 knee replacement when he was her primary caregiver for two weeks.

interests: First United Methodist church on Division Street
personality_mini_profile.communication_style: Texts in full, properly-punctuated sentences, often with a stray double-space or all-caps emphasis word. Uses 'Love, Mom' or a single heart emoji as a sign-off. Calls instead of texts for anything important — texts are mostly grocery additions, weather warnings, or short check-ins. Will send a photo of something broken with the caption 'when you get a chance.'

shared_activities: Sunday noon-to-5 dinner at her house
Rickey servicing her snowblower, lawnmower, and any failing appliance
Occasional Christmas Eve service together at First United Methodist
December gift exchange and joint trip to cousin Brian's
social_circle.communication_frequency: daily — short texts most days plus standing Tuesday and Thursday evening phone calls
recent_text_topics: Mother's Day logistics earlier this month — Rickey took her to brunch and she's been texting thank-you follow-ups and a photo of the hanging basket he bought her.
Her dishwasher started leaving residue on the top rack; she sent two photos last week and asked when he could swing by.
Asking him to pick up her prescription at the CVS on Market Street because her supplemental policy mailed the wrong card again.
A forwarded photo of Aunt Bev's grandkids at a recital and her usual one-line commentary ('Look how big!').
Confirming the menu for this coming Sunday (she's making the pot roast he likes) and asking if he can bring two quarts of milk.
social_circle.evidence_from_interview: Q05: 'The most important family member is my mom, Linda. She's 64, retired from the medical billing job two years ago, lives about fifteen minutes from me on the south side of Amsterdam... She calls me Tuesday and Thursday evenings, pretty much like clockwork.' Q15: 'Sunday is mom day — I'm at her place by noon, home by 5.' Q35: 'I took two weeks off work to be her primary support during recovery.' Q103: 'Medical billing specialist... She was meticulous — clearly where I get it.'

social_circle.name: Marcus Delano

demographics.occupation: Residential electrician (journeyman) at a small electrical contractor in Johnstown, NY
demographics.location: Johnstown, NY (rents a small house with a finished basement he uses as a music room)
demographics.education: Associate's degree in electrical technology, Fulton-Montgomery Community College, 2014

background.how_they_met: Met as classmates in the same FMCC electrical technology cohort in 2012; sat next to each other in a motor controls lab and have been inseparable since.
background.why_close: Same trade, same dry sense of humor, same conviction that you should be able to fix the thing in front of you. They've held each other through Marcus's divorce in 2020 and Rickey's grief over Wayne and breakup with Hannah. Weekly guitar nights are the ballast of both their weeks.

key_traits: the friend who shows up with a truck
interests: bluegrass and old-time music (Tony Rice, Doc Watson)
deer hunting on his uncle's land
tinkering with a beater Chevy K10
personality_mini_profile.communication_style: Texts in lowercase with no punctuation, heavy on 'lol' and 'lmao,' frequent guitar-tab snippets sent as photos, the occasional 30-second voice memo of him working out a chord change. Will send a meme without context as a complete thought. Never uses emoji except for the skull 💀 when something is dumb.

shared_activities: Wednesday-night guitar sessions at Marcus's place (acoustic singer-songwriter meets bluegrass — they split the difference on John Prine and Gillian Welch)
Occasional weekend deer-rifle range trips in the fall
Trading off helping each other on big repairs (Marcus did the panel work for Rickey's squat-rack outlet in March)
Beers at Druthers in Saratoga every couple of months
social_circle.communication_frequency: daily to near-daily — texts scattered through the workday plus a flurry every Tuesday evening confirming Wednesday plans
recent_text_topics: Picking the setlist for Wednesday — Marcus has been pushing a Tyler Childers tune and Rickey keeps countering with a Gillian Welch one.
Rickey vented about a stubborn Sub-Zero compressor diagnosis last Thursday; Marcus's response was 'pay you to walk away from it.'
Marcus is shopping for a used resonator and has been spamming Rickey with Reverb listings for opinions.
A running thread about Rickey's Acadia photos — Marcus picked his favorite (the foggy Bass Harbor headland frame) and demanded a print.
Coordinating a Saturday in early June to drive up to a guitar shop in Saratoga and grab dinner after.
social_circle.evidence_from_interview: Q07: 'My closest friend is Marcus — we went to FMCC together, he's an electrician now in Johnstown. We play guitar together once a week, usually Wednesdays at his place... He's a bluegrass guy, I'm more into the acoustic singer-songwriter stuff... We meet in the middle on John Prine and old Gillian Welch tunes.' Q15: 'Wednesdays Marcus and I play guitar.' Q44: 'I leaned harder on Marcus' during the November 2025 grief stretch. Q108: 'still be playing guitar with Marcus on Wednesdays.'

social_circle.name: Joelle Aronson

demographics.occupation: Reference librarian and adult-programming coordinator at the Albany Public Library
demographics.education: MLIS, University at Albany SUNY; undergraduate in art history

background.how_they_met: Met three years ago at a gallery opening at the Albany Museum of Art when they both got stuck staring at the same Sebastião Salgado print for ten minutes and started talking.
background.why_close: She's the smartest person in his close circle and the one who reliably pushes him intellectually — on photography, on race, on the books he should be reading next. She organizes the quarterly photography meetup that anchors his cultural life, and she's the friend who treats his anxiety as ordinary rather than fragile.

key_traits: politically engaged in a practical way
good at asking the question that reframes a problem
interests: documentary photography (especially Salgado, Mary Ellen Mark, LaToya Ruby Frazier)
antiracist book groups she runs at the library
personality_mini_profile.communication_style: Long, well-composed texts in full sentences, often with a book or article link attached. Uses em-dashes correctly. Will send a single, dry one-word reply ('Lol.') when something is unserious, and a thoughtful paragraph when it isn't. Occasional voice notes when she's walking to the bus.

shared_activities: Quarterly Albany Museum of Art photography meetup she organizes
Trading book recommendations (she put Caste in his hands; he gave her Wendell Berry)
Coffee at Stacks Espresso in Albany before or after meetups
Reviewing each other's photo edits — she's the only person whose eye Rickey fully trusts on his work
recent_text_topics: Rickey sent her his full Acadia contact sheet last month and she's been giving him sequenced feedback frame by frame.
She invited him to a small letterpress demo at her library on May 30; he's likely going.
Ongoing thread about a NYRB essay on rural photography she sent two weeks ago — he finally read it on the truck Tuesday and texted three paragraphs back.
She's been gently nudging him toward submitting to a Capital Region juried show in the fall; he's resistant but softening.
A running joke about Rickey's @barham.silvergelatin caption discipline (she thinks his captions are 'too modest by half').
social_circle.evidence_from_interview: Q07: 'a photography meetup that gathers at the Albany Museum of Art quarterly — Joelle organizes it, she's a librarian, smart as hell... we both got stuck looking at the same Salgado print for like ten minutes and started talking.' Q30: 'Joelle has been the most actively engaged — she runs antiracist book groups at her library.'

social_circle.name: Pete Halloran

demographics.occupation: Physical therapist at a sports-medicine clinic in Queensbury, NY
demographics.location: Queensbury, NY (just north of Glens Falls)
demographics.education: Doctor of Physical Therapy, Russell Sage College

background.how_they_met: Met about five years ago when Rickey started showing up to Glens Falls Trail Runners Saturday long runs; Pete was the regular who slowed down to keep him company on his first nine-miler.
background.why_close: Pete is the friend Rickey talks to about his body — back, ankle, the works — and the one who pushed him toward smarter mobility work after the October 2024 sprain. They share the Adirondacks, an evidence-based mindset, and a willingness to do a hard run in bad weather.

personality_mini_profile.communication_style: Short texts, mostly logistics — 'lot at 7:55?' or 'rain holding, going.' Sends Strava links and elevation profiles. Uses the thumbs-up reaction more than words. Occasional longer messages when something nags at him (a knee question, a route idea).

shared_activities: Saturday 8-10 a.m. long trail run with the Glens Falls Trail Runners
Tuesday/Thursday 6 p.m. group runs
Coordinating Adirondack High Peaks day hikes in summer
Quick pre- or post-run coffee at Rock Hill Bakehouse
recent_text_topics: Plotting the summer's High Peaks list — Pete needs Allen and Cliff; Rickey is along for both.
Pete prescribed a new posterior-chain warm-up after Rickey complained about residual ankle stiffness on hills; daily check-ins on whether Rickey actually did it.
Discussing the new lifting program Rickey started in March and how to fit it around Tuesday runs without trashing his legs.
Coordinating a carpool to a 25K trail race in Saratoga on June 14 they both signed up for.
Rickey sent a sunrise frame from the pedestrian bridge last weekend; Pete's reply was just 'sick.'
social_circle.evidence_from_interview: Q07: 'There's the Glens Falls Trail Runners group, maybe ten people I see regularly on Saturday runs, and a couple of guys from that, Pete and Dave, I'd call real friends.' Q15: 'Tuesdays and Thursdays I have a standing 6 p.m. trail run with the group... Saturday morning is the long trail run, 8 to 10 a.m.' Q33: ankle sprain context. Q44: leaned harder on running friends through the November grief stretch.

social_circle.name: Brian Schuyler

demographics.occupation: Independent general contractor (residential remodels and small commercial buildouts)
demographics.education: BOCES carpentry program; some coursework at Hudson Valley Community College

background.how_they_met: First cousins — Brian is Aunt Bev and Uncle Ray's older son. Grew up doing summer cookouts and Adirondack day hikes with Uncle Ray as the ringleader.
background.why_close: Both are tradesmen in their thirties navigating the path from W-2 to running their own thing. Brian made the self-employment leap five years ago, so he's Rickey's closest case study and informal advisor on the business launch. Brian crashes on Rickey's couch ~2x/year for Amsterdam-area jobs and is Rickey's December holiday host.

key_traits: self-deprecating about his own business mistakes
the cousin who tells you what something actually costs
personality_mini_profile.communication_style: Casual texts with frequent typos he doesn't bother to fix. Heavy use of 'bro,' the crying-laughing emoji, and the occasional photo of a wall he just opened up with the caption 'guess what we found.' Will call instead of text when it's actually important — usually from a truck on speakerphone.

shared_activities: Brian crashing on Rickey's couch ~2x/year when working a job near Amsterdam
December holiday visit at Brian's place in Schenectady
Aunt Bev and Uncle Ray's Thanksgivings in Gloversville
Trading trade-business advice — insurance, pricing, dealing with slow-paying clients
Watching Bills games together when schedules and travel align
recent_text_topics: Rickey ran his $35K business-launch target past Brian last month; Brian's reply was a long voice memo saying double it for the first 18 months of slow.
Brian's recommending a specific general-liability broker out of Latham he's used for five years.
Joking thread about Uncle Ray's latest political email forward after Easter — they cope-laugh together about it.
Brian asked if he can crash the couch the second weekend of June for a kitchen remodel in Rotterdam.
Bills schedule dropped last week; they've already picked the two games they'll watch together in the fall.
